feedback:
Judged from earlier races only. The candidate is iteration 6's design (score 929.37, the best raced so far) with one change: base_speed 1.0 to 1.1. Everything else is unchanged: light body (mass 0.5, body_length 0.12), wheel_track 0.12, kp 4.5, ki 0.02, kd 1.0, sensors at y 0.08 with x spread ±0.05, sensor_size 0.016, line_loss last_direction. All values are inside the contract ranges.

The evidence: in iteration 6, all three tracks finished 20/20. Oval took 2.36 s, s-bend 2.45 s and slalom 2.66 s. Slalom max_error was 0.0215 against the 0.06 m off-track limit, so there is margin. Iteration 6 also showed that lighter mass and a shorter body fixed the slalom that failed in iterations 3 to 5 (mean progress about 0.63 to 0.68, 19/20 off-track). Iteration 5 showed that oval time scales with speed (2.14 s at 1.1 with the heavier body, 2.10 s at 1.0 with wheel_track 0.10). So a 10% speed increase should save roughly 0.1 to 0.15 s per track, worth about 2 to 3 points. That is a small gain on a score already near its ceiling. The main risk is that the slalom's sharp bends at higher speed push max_error toward the limit. Iteration 3 at speed 1.1 failed the slalom, but it was on the heavier body, so that evidence is only partly relevant.

What to do after the race: if slalom completion falls below 20/20 or slalom max_error rises well above about 0.03, revert base_speed to 1.0, since the final unseen track is a different shape and robustness matters more than 2 points. If all tracks finish and completion_time falls by about 0.1 s, keep 1.1. The next lever is steering_oscillation: if it stays low (about 0.2 to 0.27), kd could drop slightly (for example 1.0 to 0.9) to reduce lag, one change at a time. Line-loss events (one per run, about 15 points at most) are not addressed by gains here, so do not spend runs on them unless a later race shows the loss is avoidable.
requested_changes: If slalom completion is below 20/20 or slalom max_error rises above about 0.03 (iteration 6 value 0.0215), revert base_speed to 1.0, because the slalom is the only track where speed has been shown to matter.

If all tracks finish and completion_time drops by about 0.1 s per track with max_error stable, keep base_speed 1.1 and test kd 0.9 with kp 4.5, since iteration 6 steering_oscillation (0.17 to 0.27) suggests there is room to reduce damping lag.

Do not change the sensor layout or line_loss on the next iteration: sensor y is at its maximum 0.08, and the single line-loss event per run (iterations 3 to 6) has not responded to any gain or geometry change.
